extracted.intended_audience: Analysts and decisionmakers in Executive Branch federal agencies preparing benefit-cost, cost-effectiveness, lease-purchase, asset valuation, or regulatory impact analyses for submission to OMB
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for conducting benefit-cost and cost-effectiveness analyses (including discounting, uncertainty, distributional effects, and lease-purchase analysis) to support Federal program, regulatory, investment, and asset-sale decisions. Specifies required methods, assumptions to report, and discount rates for analyses submitted to OMB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Benefit-Cost Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefit-cost analysis is recommended as the technique to use in a formal economic analysis of government programs or projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost-effectiveness analysis is less comprehensive and appropriate when benefits are identical across alternatives or cannot be monetized. Appendix A defines technical terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Net Present Value as Standard Criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard criterion for deciding whether a government program can be justified on economic principles is net present value -- the discounted monetized value of expected net benefits (benefits minus costs). Programs with positive net present value increase social resources and are generally preferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute by assigning monetary values to benefits and costs, discounting future items using appropriate discount rate, and subtracting discounted costs from discounted benefits. When not computable, use comprehensive enumeration and other summary measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Supplementary Effectiveness Measures
rubrics_metrics.description: When net present value is not computable or does not capture distributional effects, report comprehensive enumeration of benefits/costs, quantified physical measures where possible, and other summary effectiveness measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: injuries prevented per dollar (present value terms), internal rate of return. Quantifying benefits/costs is worthwhile even if monetary valuation is infeasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-Effectiveness Decision Criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: A program is cost-effective if, on the basis of life cycle cost analysis of competing alternatives, it has the lowest costs expressed in present value terms for a given amount of benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate when alternatives have same annual benefits or when benefits cannot be monetized. Can also be used when costs are identical but benefits differ (choose largest discounted benefits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy Rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: The rationale for the Government program being examined should be clearly stated in the analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain whether program addresses market failure (public goods, externalities) or improves government internal operations (cost-saving investments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit Assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses should be explicit about the underlying assumptions used to arrive at estimates of future benefits and costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include statement of assumptions, rationale, review of strengths and weaknesses. Report key data and year-by-year estimates to promote independent review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of Alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses should consider alternative means of achieving program objectives by examining different program scales, different methods of provision, and different degrees of government involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For capital asset acquisition consider: (i) doing nothing; (ii) direct purchase; (iii) upgrading/renovating/sharing/converting existing property; (iv) leasing or contracting for services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification and Retrospective Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Retrospective studies to determine whether anticipated benefits and costs have been realized are potentially valuable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should have a plan for periodic, results-oriented evaluation of program effectiveness and discuss relevant evaluation studies when proposing reauthorizations or increased funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Net Benefits as Basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses should include comprehensive estimates of the expected benefits and costs to society; social net benefits, not benefits/costs to the Federal Government, should be the basis for evaluating programs that affect private citizens or other governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize differences from private benefits due to externalities, monopoly power, taxes/subsidies. Use established definitions and practices for program/policy evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify Tangible and Intangible Benefits and Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Both intangible and tangible benefits and costs should be recognized; the relevant cost concept is broader than private-sector production/compliance costs or government cash expenditures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs should reflect opportunity cost measured by return in most productive alternative. Include guidance on incremental costs vs sunk costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incremental Benefits and Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculation of net present value should be based on incremental benefits and costs; sunk costs and realized benefits should be ignored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly record displaced activities as costs or record only incremental gains. Past experience relevant only for estimating future values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider Interactive Effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Possible interactions between the benefits and costs being analyzed and other government activities should be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: policies affecting agricultural output should reflect real economic values rather than subsidized prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report International Effects Separately
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses should focus on benefits and costs accruing to U.S. citizens in determining net present value; programs with effects outside the U.S. should report those effects separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude Pure Transfers from NPV
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no economic gains from a pure transfer payment because benefits to receivers are matched by costs to payers; transfers should be excluded from net present value calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify transfers that arise as a result of the program and discuss their distributional effects; recognize that transfers can have inefficiencies in delivery and financing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Willingness-to-Pay and Market Prices
rubrics_metrics.description: The principle of willingness-to-pay provides an aggregate measure of what individuals are willing to forego to obtain a benefit; market prices are an invaluable starting point for measuring willingness-to-pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When market prices are distorted or unavailable, employ other valuation methods. Measures derived from actual market behavior are preferred when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Consumer Surplus When Determinable
rubrics_metrics.description: Consumer surplus measures the extra value consumers derive beyond market price and, when determinable, provides the best measure of total benefit to society from a government program or project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consumer surplus may be calculated using econometric methods to estimate demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer Indirect Market-Consistent Measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Willingness-to-pay can sometimes be estimated indirectly (land values, wage variations); such measures are most reliable when based on actual transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures should be consistent with basic economic principles and replicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do Not Include Employment/Output Multipliers in Social Benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Employment or output multipliers that purport to measure secondary effects of government expenditures should not be included in measured social benefits or costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses should treat resources as likely to be fully employed; multipliers >1 require existence of involuntary unemployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Inflation — Real vs Nominal Consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysts should avoid making general inflation assumptions when possible; analyses are often most readily accomplished using real (constant-dollar) values. Nominal and real values must not be combined in the same analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If future benefits/costs are given in nominal terms, use those values rather than converting to constant dollars in some cases (e.g., lease-purchase). Convert consistently as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended Inflation Assumption
rubrics_metrics.description: When a general inflation assumption is needed, use the rate of increase in the GDP deflator from the Administration's economic assumptions for the period of analysis, extending beyond six-year horizon using the sixth year forecast rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administration's economic forecast is updated twice annually; alternative credible private forecasts may be used for sensitivity analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discount All Future Benefits and Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: All future benefits and costs, including nonmonetized ones, should be discounted to compute net present value; discounting reflects the time value of money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher discount rates reduce present value of future flows. Technical guidance and discount factors are in Appendix B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real vs Nominal Discount Rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a real discount rate for constant-dollar (real) benefits and costs and a nominal discount rate reflecting expected inflation for nominal benefits and costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A real discount rate can be approximated by subtracting expected inflation from a nominal interest rate; market interest rates are nominal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base-Case Discount Rate for Public Investments and Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Constant-dollar benefit-cost analyses of proposed investments and regulations should report net present value and other outcomes using a real discount rate of 7 percent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approximates the marginal pretax rate of return on an average private-sector investment; significant changes will be reflected in future updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report Sensitivity to Alternative Discount Rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses should show sensitivity of NPV and other outcomes to variations in the discount rate; the importance depends on economic characteristics of the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For proposals whose main cost is reduced business investment, also calculate NPV using higher discount rate. Internal rate of return may be reported as supplementary information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Shadow Price of Capital
rubrics_metrics.description: Using the shadow price of capital to value benefits and costs is analytically preferred to capture effects of government projects on private resource allocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate use requires computing how benefits/costs affect allocation of private consumption and investment; OMB concurrence required to use in place of base-case 7% rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treasury Rates for Cost-Effectiveness, Lease-Purchase, Internal Investments, Asset Sales
rubrics_metrics.description: Treasury borrowing rates should be used as discount rates in cost-effectiveness analyses of constant-dollar costs, nominal lease-purchase analyses, internal government investment analyses, and in asset sale analyses as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Real Treasury rates for constant-dollar cost-effectiveness (remove expected inflation); nominal Treasury rates for nominal lease payments; use comparable maturity. Appendix C provides tables and is updated annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal Government Investment Discounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal investments that provide internal benefits (increased Federal revenues or decreased Federal costs) should be evaluated using comparable-maturity Treasury rates as discount rates. Mixed projects should be allocated between Treasury rate for Federal savings and 7% real for external benefits when allocation is possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If allocation possible, discount Federal cost savings and associated costs at Treasury rate and external social benefits/costs at 7% real.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asset Sale Valuation Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Net present value to the Federal Government of holding an asset is best measured by discounting future earnings using a Treasury rate; analyses should deduct expected defaults/delays and consider probabilities of impairment or obsolescence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider that private purchasers discount earnings at rates above Treasury to reflect risk; when evidence shows private sector efficiency gains, include sensitivity comparisons discounting returns at private-sector risk rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterize and Report Uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimates of benefits and costs are typically uncertain; analyses should characterize sources and nature of uncertainty and report key information such as sources, expected-value estimates, sensitivity, and probability distributions where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use objective probability estimates when possible, market data to estimate risks, stochastic simulation methods, and report basis for distributional assumptions and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Expected Values Appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: The expected values of distributions of benefits, costs and net benefits should be used (weighting each outcome by its probability). If point estimates are used, the expected value (an unbiased estimate) is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide estimates that differ from expected values (worst-case, best-case) only with clear rationale and identification of possible bias; consider historical tendencies for cost growth or optimism bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity Analysis Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Major assumptions should be varied and NPV and other outcomes recomputed to determine sensitivity to changes in assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sensitivity analysis should consider at least: (i) benefits and costs; (ii) discount rate; (iii) general inflation rate; (iv) distributional assumptions. Document models and make available for independent review where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Adjustments for Risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Variability of risky outcomes matters relative to other determinants (e.g., real national income); variations in discount rate are generally not appropriate to adjust NPV for project-specific risk. Consider certainty-equivalents where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate certainty-equivalents to adjust uncertain expected values for risk when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze Incidence and Distributional Effects
rubrics_metrics.description: When benefits and costs have significant distributional effects, these effects should be analyzed and discussed along with NPV; indicate whether gainers could compensate losers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distributional analysis may group recipients by income quintiles, region, demographic group, industry, or occupation. Identify gainers and losers and effects on assignment of property rights. For targeted programs, assess effectiveness at reaching intended subgroup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine Economic Incidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses should identify economic incidence — how costs and benefits are ultimately borne by households or individuals rather than intermediate entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize redistribution and indirect effects (e.g., subsidies raising supplier incomes but also benefiting consumers through lower prices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Investment Excess Burden Adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation of results for public investments not justified on cost-saving grounds should include a supplementary analysis with a 25 percent excess burden (multiply public expenditure costs by 1.25 and recompute NPV).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If specific information indicates a different excess burden, provide explanation. Examples: user-charged investments (excess burden zero) or projects with both Federal savings and external benefits where portions may be exempted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lease-Purchase Coverage Tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Lease-purchase analysis applies only if (a) the lease concerns a capital asset leased for 3+ years or meets other specified life/use criteria; and (b) the asset(s) fair market value exceeds $1 million.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage tests include new assets with economic life <3 years leased for ≥75% of life, assets built to be leased, special-purpose installations, and combined asset groups exceeding $1 million.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Justification for Leases
rubrics_metrics.description: All leases of capital assets must be justified as preferable to direct government purchase and ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify via: (1) separate lease-purchase analysis (needed for major acquisitions); (2) periodic generic analyses for recurrent similar leases; or (3) formal agency policy for smaller leases submitted to OMB with demonstration that the policy yields equivalent decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Life-Cycle Cost Comparison for Lease-Purchase
rubrics_metrics.description: Lease-purchase analyses should compare the net discounted present value of the life-cycle cost of leasing with the full costs of buying/constructing an identical asset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full purchase costs include purchase price plus net present value of relevant ancillary services. Use appropriate discount rates per Section 8.c.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions for Lease-Purchase Analyses (Economic Life, Purchase Price)
rubrics_metrics.description: Economic life: remaining/productive lifetime beginning at acquisition and ending at retirement; Purchase price: fair market value a willing buyer would pay in a competitive market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economic life often differs from tax useful life. For government-owned or donated property, estimate an imputed purchase price per guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Taxes and Ancillary Services in Lease Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Normal payment of taxes on lessor income should not be subtracted from lease costs because they are reflected in purchase cost; costs of special tax benefits should be added to lease cost. Ancillary services included in lease terms should have their present value added to purchase price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of ancillary services: acquisition/preparation costs, repair/improvement costs (if in lease), operation/maintenance costs (if in lease), imputed property taxes, imputed insurance premiums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimating Imputed Costs (Purchase Price, Property Taxes, Insurance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for estimating imputed costs: imputed purchase price based on comparable market sales; imputed property taxes via local tax rates or effective tax rates times fair market value; imputed insurance from local estimates for similar property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply inflation adjustments to first-year tax/assessed values where no basis for future changes; use Building Owners and Managers Association sources where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimating Residual Value and Renewal Options
rubrics_metrics.description: Residual value is estimate of price property could be sold for at end of analysis period (present value terms); include renewal options by adding all renewal periods to initial lease period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate residual value using comparable market sales, industry/book resale estimates, or assessed values for comparable properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation and OMB Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Economic analyses submitted to OMB will be reviewed for conformity with Items 5 to 13 in this Circular through submission processes (Circular No. A-11 and A-19).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must follow these guidelines in analyses submitted to OMB in support of legislative and budget programs; effective immediately as of the circular's date.
